questions.question: Was `make e2e` against the 3P file alone run three times locally and the maximum observed wall-clock recorded in the epic completion notes? Cite the recorded numbers.

If any of the three runs exceeded 720s, was numRuns reduced to 12 (or maxCommands to 8), the validation repeated, and the chosen final value captured in a code comment beside the numRuns literal? If no breach, is that explicitly recorded? Cite the comment or note.

Is the CI envelope expectation documented (3P runtime appears in post-merge log within the same envelope; first-merge warning acceptable; sustained ≥3-merge breach triggers a follow-up)? Cite the note.

Does `git diff --stat` over the epic show NO changes under src/marmot/, src/store/, or src/components/ — only e2e/tests/multi-user-3p.property.spec.ts, optional additive two-party.ts exports, docs/two-party-permutation-matrix.md, and this epic's specs/ dir? Cite the diff.
Is e2e/tests/multi-user.property.spec.ts unmodified by this epic? Cite git diff for that path showing no change.
Is e2e/tests/three-party.spec.ts not deleted, renamed, or .skip-ed (the example-based three-party tests remain)? Cite the file's continued presence and absence of .skip.
Is `make test` (L1/L2) unaffected, and does `make e2e` run the 3P file as part of the suite (no Makefile/config change needed beyond auto-discovery)? Cite evidence.

Was the one-shot MANUAL fault-injection validation performed (introduce a 3-party-only divergence, e.g. disable C's relay subscription, run make e2e, observe a counterexample whose chain includes a C.* command and a task event C cannot see post-quiesce, then revert) and documented in completion notes? This is manual, not an automated assertion — confirm it was done and reverted.

If runs show persistent multi-context red without a demonstrable 3-party divergence, is it treated as documented harness flakiness (project memory: multi-context e2e blanking) rather than a test defect — and is that judgment recorded with evidence rather than silently passing?
Are the wall-clock measurements and any numRuns/maxCommands tuning captured durably (completion notes + code comment) so a future maintainer can see the chosen budget and why?
